page: Microsoft Azure DC24s_v3 is a member of the DCSv3 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated physical cores and 24 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 48 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results place the DC24s_v3 in the average performance tier for most standard operations. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is 1897.99, and the multi-core score is 45527.64. In memory bandwidth tests, it achieves 164.61 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 64.58 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Geekbench testing shows an average single-core score of 1671.0 and a multi-core score of 15764.0, with a strong performance in image processing at 15333.0. Large language model inference speeds are strong for small 135M models at 306.23 tokens/sec for text generation but drop to a weak tier of 2.74 tokens/sec for large 70B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated physical core allocation and 192.0 GB memory capacity provide a stable resource density for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of hyperthreading. The absence of bundled local storage requires external storage provisioning, which represents a configuration tradeoff. This server is suited for database operations, software compilation, memory-intensive web serving, and small-scale language model inference.
